tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the user's CortexPlus memory and return ranked matches. Use this to find what the user has stored before answering from memory.

tools.name: fetch
tools.description: Retrieve the full content of one CortexPlus memory item by id, as returned by search.

tools.name: recall
tools.description: Build a context block from the user's CortexPlus memory: the passages that answer a question plus their graph neighbours, already formatted as text. Prefer this over search when you intend to answer from the user's memory.

tools.name: remember
tools.description: Store a note in the user's CortexPlus memory so future conversations can recall it.

tools.name: memory
tools.description: Save a memory in CortexPlus. CortexPlus decides whether it is a note, task, or reminder and extracts the client.

tools.name: tasks
tools.description: List open CortexPlus tasks and reminders, optionally filtered by client.

tools.name: signup
tools.description: Create a CortexPlus account, or begin signing in to an existing one, so this conversation can use CortexPlus as the user's long-term memory and knowledge base. tools.name: connect
tools.description: Complete the CortexPlus connection with the short authentication key the user received by email after signup. Ask the user to paste the key, then call this tool; never guess or invent the key. The response includes an API key that the AI platform should save in its CortexPlus connector configuration

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "search" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Search the user's CortexPlus memory and return ranked matches. Use this to find what the user has stored before answering from memory.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.
